2. The trial was held under the Special. Powers Act, 1974 which provides for an appeal under Section 30 of the said Act. Special period of limitation has been pre-scribed by section 30 of the Act for prefer-ring an appeal. The convict accused petitioners did not prefer any appeal. Since they could not prefer any appeal within time, the appeal is barred by limitation. 

 3. The learned Advocate for the accused petitioners submits that he has no alternative remedy but an application for quashing the proceedings under Section 56 IA of the Code in this court. It is now well-settled that where a special period of limitation has been prescribed by a special law, section 5 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application. Therefore whether an application under Section 561A of the Code in this court could be devised to circumvent the period of limitation provided for by the special law. To entertain this application under section 561A of the Code would amount to nutralising the special statute providing a special period of limitation under Section 30 of the Special Powers Act. Furthermore the Code had undergone a great change by recent amendments by which a question has arisen whether jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code could go to the extent of making the provision relating to the special limitation anfractuous. In this connection reference may be made to section 241A and 165C of the Code. Previously in some cases the superior courts in special circumstances had gone beyond the petition of complaint or the First Information Report and in appropriate cases interfered with the prosecution by giving reasons. Now in view of the right given to the accused under section 241A or 265C of the Code as the case may the discretionary power of the High Court Division be exercised cautiously, when the Code has given a right to the accused to raise the point on which he is entitled to be discharged or not, on perusal of the materials on record of the case by the trial court. The High Court Division to exercise the power under section 561A of the Code to go beyond the F.I.R. or the petition of complaint would make section 241A and 265C of the Code useless and delay the disposal of the case. In the circumstances it would not be proper for the High Court Division to go beyond the F.I.R. or the petition of complaint. This is with respect to pre-trial exercise of the power of the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code. 

 9. There is no dispute that the special tribunal is a special criminal tribunal and subordinate to the High Court Division. Section 29 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) pro-vides that the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the Code) shall apply so far as it is not inconsistent with the Act. Section 30 of the Act provides for an appeal to this court against any order passed by the Special Tribunal within 30 days of the passing of such order. The Act does not provide for any revision against any order passed by the Special Tribunal inasmuch as any order passed by the Special Tribunal is made appeal-able. It is now well-settled that if an appeal is provided for and a special period of limitation is provided for preferring the appeal then if the appellate forum is also the forum for revision or Miscellaneous proceedings then the period of special limitation provided for the appeal would be applicable for the revision or miscellaneous proceedings. The Special Powers Act has not provided for any revision. In section 32 of the Act it only provided for proceedings for bail and any order passed by the Special Tribunal is appealable under section 30 of the Act. Chapter XXXIX of the Code deals with bail. The instant application under section 561A of the Code has been captioned as a revision; therefore the application comes within the mischief of special limitation provided for under the Act. Even if the instant application under section 561A of the Code had been captioned as a miscellaneous application it would also be governed by the special period of limitation provided for under section 30 of the Act. In the circumstances the instant application is barred by limitation. The High Court Division cannot in the exercise of its inherent power act in contravention of law. The special law (i.e. the Act) having pro-vided an appeal by which a conviction recorded by a Special Tribunal within a special period of limitation to set aside the conviction the High Court Division should not entertain an application under section 561A of the Code inasmuch as to entertain the said application beyond the special period of limitation would amount to entertaining a time barred appeal under Special Law in the garb of an application under Section-561A of the Code. To entertain the instant application would amount to a colourable exercise of power. That which cannot be done directly cannot equally be done indirectly. Further the appellate jurisdiction is much wider than the jurisdiction of this court under section 561A of the Code. If no appeal is preferred against the order passed by the Special Tribunal, on the expiration of the special period of limitation, the order passed by the Special Tribunal becomes final, past and closed transaction in relation to the High Court Division exercising its criminal jurisdiction. 

 10. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the instant application under section 561A of the Code is maintainable and in this connection has referred to the case of Kaushailiya reported in Supreme Court (India) Appeals Vol.1 page 53. In that case the question of special limitation was not there. In the facts of the instant ease the case referred to by Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate has no relevance. Further we have already stated that section 5 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application in case of a special period of limitation, provided for by -.the special Act. In the circumstances, we cannot invoke section 5 of the Limitation 'Act and take the mistake of the learned Advocate into consideration and entertain the instant application by exercising our -inherent power. Accordingly we find no substance on merit.
